title: Hochschild Hyperhomology and Cyclic Tensor Invariance

items.title: Hochschild hyperhomology of a bounded bimodule complex
items.statement: Let k be a field, A a unital (possibly internally graded) k-algebra, and F a bounded cochain complex of k-central A-bimodules with internal-degree-zero differentials. Put T^n(A,F)=direct-sum over i-j=n of C_j(A,F^i), j>=0, with D=d_F+(-1)^i b on the (i,j) summand, where b lowers j. Define HHhyper^n(A,F)=H^n(T). The internal grading descends; the separate i and j degrees give a filtration, not in general two homology gradings. For graded A use the ordinary Hochschild boundary without extra internal Koszul signs.
items.strategy: Show each total degree contains finitely many i because F is bounded, identify d_F and b as commuting maps, and calculate D^2: the mixed coefficients (-1)^i and (-1)^(i+1) cancel. Both maps preserve internal degree. Define cohomology and the finite decreasing i-filtration explicitly; do not identify this total cohomology with iterated homology.

references.title: Beliakova–Putyra–Wehrli, Quantum Link Homology via Trace Functor I, §§3.8.4–3.8.6, printed pp.37–39

items.title: Hochschild hyperhomology is independent of a projective resolution
items.statement: Assume AC. Reindex the two-sided bar resolution by cochain degree -p. Its tensor total with F has degree-n terms ⊕_{i-p=n} Bar_p(A)⊗_{A^e}F^i. The bar-to-Hochschild map rescaled by (-1)^(ip) identifies the standard tensor differential b+(-1)^p d_F with D=d_F+(-1)^i b. Every supplied bounded-above projective right-A^e resolution computes the same hyperhomology; quasi-isomorphisms of bounded coefficient complexes induce internal-degree-preserving isomorphisms when homogeneous of degree zero.
items.strategy: Use the bar-to-Hochschild chain isomorphism with the explicit (-1)^(ip) sign check. Bar terms are right-A^e projective under AC; compare any supplied projective resolution with the reindexed bar by the published comparison and homotopy-uniqueness theorem, then tensor homotopies with F. For a coefficient quasi-isomorphism, tensor its bounded acyclic cone with the bounded-above flat bar resolution. Each total diagonal is finite because F is bounded.

references.title: Beliakova–Putyra–Wehrli, Quantum Link Homology via Trace Functor I, §3.8.6, printed p.38

items.title: Termwise Hochschild homology and iterated homology
items.statement: For each j>=0 and a bounded cochain complex F of k-central A-bimodules, the bimodule differential induces a cochain differential HH_j(A,d_F^i):HH_j(A,F^i)→HH_j(A,F^(i+1)). Define its cohomology H^i(HH_j(A,F)). If A and F are internally graded, retain i, Hochschild degree j, and internal degree separately. This is not defined to equal HHhyper^(i-j)(A,F).
items.strategy: A bimodule map commutes with every Hochschild face, hence induces a chain map on Hochschild chains and a map on HH_j. Apply this to d_F; its square induces zero because d_F^2=0. The induced map preserves internal grading. Define the iterated cohomology of this bounded cochain complex without invoking the AC-qualified published coefficient long-exact-sequence theorem.

references.title: Beliakova–Putyra–Wehrli, Quantum Link Homology via Trace Functor I, §§3.8.4–3.8.6, printed pp.37–39

items.title: Termwise Hochschild homology respects bimodule chain homotopies
items.statement: For bounded cochain complexes F,G of k-central A-bimodules, bimodule-linear cochain maps f,g with a bimodule-linear cochain homotopy f-g=d_G h+h d_F induce cochain-homotopic maps on HH_j(A,F^i) for every j, hence the same maps on H^i(HH_j(A,F)). Thus a bimodule chain-homotopy equivalence induces isomorphisms on all iterated groups. No invariance under arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms is asserted.
items.strategy: Check HH_j(A,-) is additive: Hochschild chain maps for f+g are degreewise sums, so their maps on cycles and quotients add. Apply HH_j to the homotopy equation, obtaining HH_j(f)-HH_j(g)=HH_j(d_G)HH_j(h)+HH_j(h)HH_j(d_F), with h lowering cochain degree. Pass to cohomology and then apply to the two homotopies of an equivalence. No projective resolution or choice is needed.

items.title: Termwise Hochschild spectral sequence of a bounded bimodule complex
items.statement: For a bounded cochain complex F of k-central A-bimodules, the decreasing filtration F^pT^n=direct-sum over i>=p and i-j=n of C_j(A,F^i) gives a natural cohomological spectral sequence E_1^(i,-j)=HH_j(A,F^i), E_2^(i,-j)=H^i(HH_j(A,F)), with d_r:E_r^(i,-j)→E_r^(i+r,-j-r+1), abutting to the finite image filtration on HHhyper^(i-j)(A,F). The same holds in each internal degree. Higher differentials and extension problems may occur.
items.strategy: The differential b preserves i while d_F raises it, so associated-graded differential is (-1)^i b and E_1 is HH_j. The first-page differential is induced by d_F; hence E_2 is the iterated group. Each T^n has a finite i-filtration because F is bounded, even though j is unbounded across all total degrees. Apply the published cohomological reindexing and degreewise finite-filtration abutment theorem; do not invoke a first-quadrant theorem for negative Hochschild index.

items.title: Double bar comparison for cyclic bimodule tensor products
items.statement: Assume AC; M is finite projective as a right B-module and N finite projective as a right A-module. P_A=Bar(A)⊗_A(M⊗_B N) and Q_A=Tot(Bar(A)⊗_A M⊗_B Bar(B)⊗_B N), with homological total differential d_A+(-1)^p d_B, are projective right-A^e resolutions of M⊗_B N; the exchanged models resolve N⊗_A M over B^e. After enveloping coinvariants the middle double bars rotate by (-1)^(pq); the outer comparisons give a natural-up-to-homotopy, involutive-up-to-homotopy equivalence of Hochschild complexes and hence isomorphic HH_j. No left-projectivity is asserted.
items.strategy: Use finite right-projective retracts to show M⊗_B N is right-A projective and N⊗_A M right-B projective. For each double-bar bidegree, retain the middle vector space A^⊗p⊗M⊗B^⊗q and use AC bases plus projectivity of the outer right module to prove right-enveloping projectivity. The B-bar augmentation is exact after tensor with M because M is right-B flat; first-quadrant assembly and the outer bar contraction give the resolutions. Check both bar differential signs and balance relations for rotation after coinvariants, then compare projective resolutions under AC⇒DC.

references.title: Beliakova–Putyra–Wehrli, Quantum Link Homology via Trace Functor I, §3.8.4, printed pp.37–39

items.title: Derived cyclicity of Hochschild hyperhomology
items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded complexes M of (A,B)-bimodules with finite projective right-B terms and N of (B,A)-bimodules with finite projective right-A terms, the ordinary signed tensor totals compute both derived tensor products. Their Hochschild hyperhomology groups are naturally internally graded isomorphic in every total degree. On the middle double-bar coinvariant models, swapping blocks of cochain-bar degrees i-p and l-q carries sign (-1)^((i-p)(l-q)); the rotation squares to the identity, while the outer projective-resolution comparisons are homotopy equivalences. No left-projectivity or arbitrary-projective-target derived-functor claim is made.
items.strategy: Termwise right projectivity makes the ordinary signed tensors valid derived models. Build the two standard double-bar resolutions and use the explicit double-bar lemma for projectivity, augmentation quasi-isomorphisms, and finite-diagonal convergence. Identify their coinvariants with hyperhomology through the common triple bar total. Swap the grouped blocks of degrees i-p and l-q and check the two grouped differential components; AC supplies bar bases and comparison choices. The rotation is a strict involution on middle coinvariants.

items.title: Termwise Hochschild cyclicity for bounded projective bimodule complexes
items.statement: Assume AC and the same right-sided finite projectivity hypotheses on bounded graded M and N as in derived cyclicity. For every Hochschild degree j, cochain degree r and internal degree, there is a natural isomorphism H^r(HH_j(A,Tot(M⊗_B N)))≅H^r(HH_j(B,Tot(N⊗_A M))). It comes from a cochain isomorphism after applying HH_j termwise, using (-1)^(il) to swap M^i and N^l. This is a separate iterated-homology result and is not inferred from a hyperhomology abutment.
items.strategy: Apply the natural HH_j cyclicity furnished by the double-bar lemma to each (M^i,N^l). Finite tensor diagonals and additivity of HH_j identify HH_j of a finite direct sum with the sum of the pairwise groups. On the (i,l) summand multiply the pairwise rotation by (-1)^(il). Naturality gives compatibility with d_M and d_N; explicitly the M-term gains (-1)^l after swapping and the N-term coefficient (-1)^i cancels against the change from il to i(l+1). Thus the map commutes with the cochain differentials before cohomology. Reverse rotation gives its inverse, with the square sign (-1)^(2il)=1. AC is inherited from the double-bar projective comparison.

title: Hochschild Hyperhomology and Cyclic Tensor Invariance — Examples

items.title: Total and separate Hochschild degrees for a two-term complex
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R=k[x] with internal degree of x equal to 2, and take F^0=R, F^1=R{4}, all other terms zero, with zero cochain differential. The four nonzero termwise groups are HH_0(R,F^0)=R, HH_1(R,F^0)=R{2}, HH_0(R,F^1)=R{4}, and HH_1(R,F^1)=R{6}. Their (i,j,internal) degrees project to total cochain degrees 0,-1,1,0 respectively. In this zero-differential example the E_2 page already gives the total hyperhomology, but the separate i,j decomposition is only a filtration in general.
items.strategy: Use the published one-variable diagonal Koszul computation and shift naturality to calculate each termwise group. Place the four entries at (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1), write the total degrees i-j, and observe that both horizontal and vertical differentials vanish in the short Koszul model. Read the total groups degree by degree; distinguish this special collapse from the general spectral-sequence theorem. AC is required only by the cited polynomial Hochschild theorem.

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Chapter 9, §9.1, printed pp.300–304

items.title: Matrix-unit rotation for a k–Mat_n(k) Morita pair
items.statement: For A=k, B=Mat_n(k), M=k^(1×n) and N=k^(n×1), multiplication gives M⊗_B N≅k and N⊗_k M≅B. The rotation sends [e_i⊗e_j^T] to [e_j^T⊗e_i], which multiplication identifies with E_(ji); its trace δ_ij equals the row-column scalar product e_i e_j^T=δ_ij. Thus HH_0 identifies through trace, and higher HH groups agree by the general bar comparison.
items.strategy: Split the first-row map M←B by v↦e_1^T v, whose matrix has first row v, to prove right-B projectivity. Verify both tensor products by explicit balance relations and basis-to-basis multiplication. Compute [B,B]=ker(tr) using matrix-unit commutators, with no division by n, and compare the rotated degree-zero classes. Use the general double-bar result for higher degrees.

items.title: A minus sign when rotating two odd cochain factors
items.statement: Assume AC. Take A=B=k=Q and let M and N each be the one-dimensional k-bimodule in cochain degree 1 only, with zero differential and internal degree 0. On the bar-degree-zero summand, cyclic rotation of m⊗n is (-1)^(1·1)n⊗m=-(n⊗m), a nontrivial minus sign over Q. Two rotations give the identity; the only surviving Hochschild degree is j=0 and total cochain degree is 2.
items.strategy: Check both ordinary derived tensor models reduce to k in cochain degree 2. The bar-degree-zero formula in the derived theorem and the (-1)^(il) termwise formula each yield -1 for i=l=1, while all differential compatibility checks are vacuous because d_M=d_N=0. Apply the ground-field Hochschild calculation for j>0 directly from the alternating bar faces. Rotating twice multiplies by (-1)^2=1; this verifies the sign instance, not the general comparison.
